summary: Current synthetic bootstrap changes are largely correct, but event sequence handling can permanently stall when globally sequenced events from other sessions interleave.
scope: Current working-tree synthetic bootstrap slice; no tracked base-to-head diff exists.

open_findings.trigger: Global app events interleave sessions: sequence 1 belongs to another session and sequence 2 belongs to the selected session.
open_findings.impact: Filtering the foreign event before the contiguous-sequence check makes sequence 2 appear to be a gap. The current-session event is withheld, the cursor stays at 0, and the UI reports reconciliation needed indefinitely. The architecture defines one monotonic app sequence.
open_findings.evidence: The filter at lines 68–75 precedes the gap check at lines 83–97. Existing mixed-session tests place foreign events after the selected session's contiguous events.
open_findings.correction: Check continuity and advance the global cursor across all valid events, then apply only events belonging to the selected session. Add an interleaved-session regression case.

prior_finding_closure.r2: Snapshot session filtering, stale status ordering, package direction/public entries, invalid-result fallback, and omitted test discovery are closed in current source.
prior_finding_closure.r3: Single-session out-of-order replay, browser-reachable Node builtin rejection, and compiled bridge build target are closed. The global-sequence interleaving case above remains uncovered.
